messages:
Maria T.: Heads-up — I'm seeing large gaps in traces for requests that go gateway -> SQS -> workers. Dashboards show a lot of isolated spans with no parent. Anyone else noticed this?
Arik: Yep saw it this morning during the 11:42 deploy. Worker spans appear as root because the sampling decision / trace headers are getting lost when we transform messages.
Sam: Confirmed. Gateway writes `traceparent` into HTTP headers, but our queue producer path only adds a single attribute sometimes and we canonicalize to the otel proto header on the sync path. The transform lambda strips unknown attrs.
Lee: FWIW older consumers still look for `b3` or `uber-trace-id`. If we only emit `traceparent` some libs ignore it. Also batching code ended up concatenating header values once and that blew up the extractor.
Maria T.: Quick proposal: emit two things when we enqueue: (1) preserve the standard `traceparent` header if present, and (2) add a compact opaque attribute `x-rdinfer-trace` that contains a tiny rehydration blob (traceparent + selected baggage keys) encoded urlsafe-base64. Workers should try normal OTEL extraction first, then fallback to `x-rdinfer-trace`. This avoids depending on downstream libs to know every propagation format.
Arik: Opaque header approach sounds good. Two concerns: baggage size and attribute size limits (SQS message attribute max is ~256 chars for StringValue). We must whitelist baggage keys (only `uid`, `rollout-flag`, `debug-id`) and drop the rest.
Sam: Also SQS attributes can't contain newlines and have limited size. Suggest compressing the small blob with zlib and then base64-url encode. If the compacted size still > 240 chars, fallback to a pointer flow (store blob in a short-lived S3 key and put `x-rdinfer-trace-s3: <key>` as attribute).
infra-bot: :information_source: deploy-bot scheduled: gateway canary (propagate_compact_trace) tomorrow 03:00 UTC.
Lee: Implementation note for gateway -> SQS producer: set MessageAttributes: { "x-rdinfer-trace": { DataType: "String", StringValue: <compact> } }. Keep `traceparent` in headers for sync handlers. Worker side: extractor order -> OTEL HTTPTextFormat.extract(headers) -> parse MessageAttributes["x-rdinfer-trace"] -> if present decode zlib+base64 and let OTEL rehydrate.
Maria T.: Example compact encoding pseudocode:
```
// sketch (node-ish)
const payload = { tp: traceparent, baggage: pick(baggage, whitelist) }
const compressed = zlib.deflateSync(JSON.stringify(payload))
const compact = base64url(compressed) // url-safe base64, no padding
// set as message attr or header
```
Sam: Tests we need: (1) propagate_trace_when_baggage_small, (2) fallback_s3_pointer_when_compact_too_big, (3) extractor_handles_missing_traceparent_but_has_x-rdinfer-trace. Add integration that runs through gateway -> SQS -> worker under canary.
Arik: About exporters/collector: when worker rehydrates and emits spans we risk duplicate parents if gateway already emitted a pre-span. We should add an attribute `rd.rehydrated=true` on rehydrated spans so we can dedupe in the OTEL pipeline or at query time. Also add `rd.trace_id` as stable id for joins.
Lee: Agreed. Collector rule: if `rd.rehydrated` then route to the same trace as parent. We should also ensure sampling decision is carried in the compact blob (sampled flag) to avoid emitting partial traces.
Maria T.: Operational items: add a telemetry coverage panel to Console: percent of requests with full trace context across gateway->queue->worker, a metric `trace_rehydrate_fallback_rate`, and an alert if rehydrate_fail_rate > 0.1%.
Sam: Rollout plan: feature flag `propagate_compact_trace` default off. Enable in dev/staging, then prod canary on 2 hosts. Watch `trace_coverage` and `rehydrate_fail_rate`. If fail rate spikes, rollback.
Arik: For S3 fallback we must TTL keys (24h) and quota the writes. We should emit metric `trace_s3_fallback_count`.
Lee: Small compatibility note: some libraries expect `traceparent` to be in HTTP headers only, not SQS attrs. We'll keep both where possible so sync routes remain untouched.
Maria T.: I'll write a short RFC / PR template tonight. Assigning owners: @Arik prototype encoder & whitelist, @Lee worker extractor + dedupe attr, @Sam tests + dashboard, infra-bot to schedule canary. ETA: can we aim for EOD Friday?
Arik: I'll prototype by Thursday noon.
Lee: I'll pick up worker changes, ETA Friday EOD.
Sam: Tests + dashboard ETA Friday EOD.
infra-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary scheduled (feature flag canary) for epoch 1767080000.
Maria T.: Thanks all, I'll post the RFC link when ready :eyes:
